# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei ist Teil des Kuratierungsprozesses: Sie enthält die inhaltlichen
Leitplanken für alle KI-generierten Texte und Diagramme. Die maschinenlesbaren
Parameter dazu stehen in `ai/policy.json`; beide werden von
`ai_workflow.py auftrag` wörtlich in jeden Regenerierungsauftrag eingebettet.
Änderungen an Policy oder Richtlinien ⇒ `version` in `policy.json` erhöhen;
`ai_workflow.py status` zeigt dann, welche Fragmente noch mit einer älteren
Version erzeugt wurden.

## Geltungsbereich und Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch (`site.json → sprachen.kanonisch`). KI-Inhalte
  werden ausschließlich deutsch erzeugt; die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter
  Schritt (i18n_*.py) und niemals Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und `[SWS_…]`-Kennungen bleiben
  in jeder Sprache unverändert.

## Strukturelle Invarianten

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai` für
  Abschnitte, `ai usage` für Verwendungshinweise an Records, `ai module-guide`
  für Modul-Leitfäden) mit Badge und abschließender `<p class="ai-note">`
  (KI-Hinweis). Bestehende Fragmente sind die Referenz.
- Fragmente liegen unter `content/ai/<seiten-verzeichnis>/` und heißen
  `rec_<ELEMENT-ID>_<NN>.html` (an ein Spezifikationselement gebunden) oder
  `main_<NN>.html` (seitenbezogen).

## Belegpflicht und Quellen

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist mit `[SWS_…]`/`[RS_…]`-Zitat zu belegen
  (`policy.zitierpflicht`); Zitate verlinken auf das Quelldokument (PDF mit
  `#nameddest`), Richtwert `policy.relevanz.min_zitate_je_absatz`.
- Es dürfen nur Dokumente aus dem Quellenregister `ai/quellen.json` verwendet
  werden. Neue Quellen werden zuerst dort registriert (id, titel, typ, url).
- Aus Quellen extrahierte Einzelaussagen, auf die sich ein Text stützt, werden
  in der Trace unter `wissen[]` festgehalten: `{"aussage": …, "quelle": <id>,
  "fundstelle": …}`.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Spezifikation schweigt, darf die KI Lücken mit Annahmen schließen —
  höchstens `policy.annahmen.budget_je_text` pro Text bzw.
  `budget_je_diagramm` pro Diagramm.
- Jede Annahme wird (a) im Text als Interpretation erkennbar formuliert und
  (b) in der Trace unter `annahmen[]` protokolliert:
  `{"annahme": …, "begruendung": …}`.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekuliert.

## Diagramm-Entscheidung

Ein Diagramm wird nur eingefügt, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet
(`policy.diagramme`):

- Sequenzdiagramm (`.seq.json`): Abläufe mit ≥ `sequenz_ab_schritten`
  Schritten oder nicht offensichtlicher Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Strukturdiagramm (`.dot`): ≥ `kontext_ab_beteiligten` beteiligte
  Komponenten oder nicht-triviale Vererbungs-/Abhängigkeitscluster.
- Zustandsdiagramm (`.dot`): Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Die Entscheidung („warum dieses Diagramm, warum diese Form“), etwaige
Annahmen und das Denk-Transkript zur Quellenerstellung gehören in die Trace
unter `diagramme["<quellpfad>"]` — nicht ins HTML. Diagrammquellen liegen als
`<fragment-stem>.<diag-id>.dot|.seq.json` neben dem Fragment (inline) bzw.
unter `diagrams/` (seitenweite Diagramme); gerendert wird mit
`render_diagrams.py`. Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert.

    {
      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P6_06",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 6,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n1 Introduction and functional overview\nThis document is the software specification of the\nState Management\nfunctional\ncluster within the\nAdaptive Platform Services\n.\nState Management\nis responsible for determination of the overall operation state of\nthe Adaptive AUTOSAR Platform. Additionally\nState Management\ntakes care to set\nComponents\ninto an internal\nComponent State\nwhich depends on the determined\nOperational State\nand on other project specific requirements. The idea behind\nComponent States\nis to control\nProcesss\nin a more fine-grained way without the\nneed of restarting them with a different set of command-line parameters.\nState Management\ninteracts with the\nExecution Management\nto request\nFunc-\ntion Groups\nand the\nMachine State\nto enter specific states that are determined\nto project requirements.\nChapter 7 describes how\nState Management\nconcepts are realized within the\nAdap-\ntive Platform\n.\nChapter 8 documents the State Management Application Programming Interface (API).\n1.1 What is State Management?\nState Management\nis the functional cluster within the\nAdaptive Platform Ser-\nvices\nthat is responsible to determine the operation state, based on information re-\nceived or gathered from other\nAdaptive Platform\nApplications or Adaptive Appli-\ncations.\n1.2 Interaction with AUTOSAR Runtime for Adaptive\nThe set of programming interfaces to the Adaptive Applications is called AUTOSAR\nRuntime for Adaptive (ARA). The interfaces that constitute ARA include those of\nState\nManagement\nspecified in Chapter 8 . Note that APIs accessed by\nState Manage-\nment\nusing the inter-functional cluster API that is described in Appendix A which is\nnot part of ARA.\nThe Adaptive AUTOSAR Services are provided via mechanisms provided by the\nCom-\nmunication Management\nfunctional cluster [1] of the Adaptive Platform Foundation\n6 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P7_07",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 7,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n2 Acronyms and Abbreviations\nThe glossary below includes acronyms and abbreviations relevant to the\nState Man-\nagement\nmodule that are not included in the AUTOSAR glossary[2]."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P7_08",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 7,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The element of\nState Management\nthat characterizes the cur-\nrent status of a set of (functionally coherent) user-level\nAppli-\ncations\n. The set of\nFunction Groups\nand their\nFunction\nGroup States\nis machine specific and are configured in the\nMachine Manifest\n[7]."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P7_09",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 7,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The element of\nState Management\nthat characterizes the cur-\nrent internal state of the\nState Management\n. The\nOpera-\ntional State\nis machine specific and depends on multiple\nevents from somewhere within the system."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P7_10",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 7,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The element of\nState Management\nthat characterizes the cur-\nrent state of\nComponents\nwithin an\nAdaptive Application\n.\nThe Component State is\nAdaptive Application\nspecific and\ntherefore it has to be described in the respective\nExecution\nManifest\n. Every\nAdaptive Application\nprovides at least\nan \"On\" and an \"Off\" State."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P8_11",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 8,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\nThe following technical terms used throughout this document are defined in the official\n[2] AUTOSAR Glossary or [7] TPS Manifest Specification  they are repeated here for\ntracing purposes."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P9_12",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 9,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n3 Related documentation\n3.1 Input documents & related standards and norms\nThe main documents that serve as input for the specification of the\nState Manage-\nment\nare:\n[1] Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR_SWS_CommunicationManagement\n[2] Glossary\nAUTOSAR_TR_Glossary\n[3] Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR_SWS_ExecutionManagement\n[4] Specification for Network Management\nAUTOSAR_SWS_NetworkManagement\n[5] Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR_SWS_Diagnostics\n[6] Specification of Update and Configuration Management\nAUTOSAR_SWS_UpdateAndConfigManagement\n[7] Specification of Manifest\nAUTOSAR_TPS_ManifestSpecification\n[8] General Specification of Basic Software Modules\nAUTOSAR_SWS_BSWGeneral\n[9] Requirements on Persistency\nAUTOSAR_RS_Persistency\n[10] Requirements of State Management\nAUTOSAR_RS_StateManagement\n3.2 Related specification\nAUTOSAR provides a General Specification on Basic Software modules [8, SWS BSW\nGeneral], which is also valid for\nState Management\n.\nThus, the specification SWS BSW General shall be considered as additional and re-\nquired specification for StateManagement\n9 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P10_13",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 10,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n4 Constraints and assumptions\n4.1 Limitations\nThis section lists known limitations of\nState Management\nand their relation to this\nrelease of the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\nwith the intent to provide an indication\nhow\nState Management\nwithin the context of the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\nwill evolve in future releases.\nThe following functionality is mentioned within this document but is not (fully) specified\nin this release:\n•\nSection 7.3\nComponent States\nare partially discussed. Information which\nshould be available from\nExecution Manifest\nto enable\nComponent\nfunc-\ntionality is not yet modeled. Model information for\nComponents\nand\nComponent\nStates\nwill be available in the next release.\n•\nSection 7.4 Communication Control for Diagnostic reasons this is not yet dis-\ncussed with\nAdaptive Diagnostics\n. It will be expanded in the next release.\n•\nSection 7.4 RequestRestart for Diagnostic reasons this is discussed with\nAdap-\ntive Diagnostics\n, but some interface details are not yet finalized. It will be\nexpanded in a next release.\n4.2 Applicability to car domains\nIf a superior\nState Management\ninstance to the one from the ECU is available in\na hierarchical car context, the\nState Management\nof the ECU shall also evaluate\nevents generated by the superior instance of\nState Management\n. Section 7.8 will\ngive further details.\n10 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P11_14",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n5 Dependencies to other modules\n5.1 Platform dependencies\n5.1.1 Operating System Interface\nState Management\nhas no direct interface to the Operating System. All OS depen-\ndencies are abstracted by the\nExecution Management\nand\nPersistency\n.\n5.1.2 Execution Manager Interface\nState Management\nis dependent on\nExecution Management\nto start and stop\nprocesses - as part of the defined\nFunction Groups\nor\nMachine States\n.\n5.1.3 Persistency\nState Management\nis dependent on the Persistency [9] functional cluster. Persis-\ntency is used to access persistent storage.\n5.1.4 Adaptive Diagnostics\nState Management\nis dependent on the\nAdaptive Diagnostics\n[5] functional\ncluster.\nAdaptive Diagnostics\nprovides information about an ongoing diagnostics\nsession. This information is evaluated by\nState Management\nto prevent shutdown\nof the system when a diagnostics session is ongoing.\n5.1.5 Update And Config Management\nState Management\nis dependent on the\nUpdate and Config Management\n[6]\nfunctional cluster.\nUpdate and Config Management\nprovides information about\nan ongoing update session. This information is evaluated by\nState Management\nto\nprevent shutdown of the system when an update session is ongoing.\n5.1.6 Network Management\nState Management\nis dependent on the\nNetwork Management\n[4] functional clus-\nter.\nNetwork Management\nprovides multiple NetworkHandle fields which represents\na set of (partial) networks.\nState Management\nevaluates this fields to set\nFunction\nGroups\nto the corresponding\nFunction Group State\ndefined in\nManifest\nand\n11 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"
    },

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n7 Functional specification\nState Management\nis a functional cluster contained in the\nAdaptive Platform\nServices\n.\nState Management\nis responsible for all aspects of Operation\nState\nManagement\nincluding handling of incoming events or requests, prioritization of these\nevents/requests and setting the\nOperational State\n. The\nState Management\ncan also register to properties of other Adaptive Platform or\nAdaptive Applica-\ntions\nto be informed about changes. These changes can also trigger a transition in\nthe\nOperational State\nmachine.\nAdditionally the\nState Management\ntakes care of not shutting down the system as\nlong as any diagnostic or update session is active as part of its internal\nOperational\nState\n.\nIn dependency of the current\nOperational States\n,\nState Management\nmight de-\ncide to request\nFunction Groups\nor\nMachine State\nto enter specific state by us-\ning interfaces of\nExecution Management\n.\nState Management\nis responsible for en- and disabling (partial) networks by means\nof\nNetwork Management\n.\nNetwork Management\nprovides ara::com fields (Net-\nworkHandle) where each of the fields represents a set of (partial) networks.\nState\nManagement\ncan influence these fields in dependency of\nFunction Groups\nstates\nand - vice versa - can set\nFunction Groups\nto a defined state depending on the\nvalue of\nNetwork Management\ns NetworkHandle fields.\nFrom the\nState Management\ninternal\nOperational States\nmore fine grained\nAdaptive Application\nand\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\nApplication internal\nstates can be derived. They are called\nComponent States\n.\nThis chapter describes the functional behaviour of\nState Management\nand the re-\nlation to other\nAdaptive Platform Applications State Management\ninteracts\nwith.\n•\nSection 7.1 presents an introduction to key terms within\nState Management\nfocusing on the relationship between\nProcesses\n,\nComponents\n,\nOperational\nStates\nand\nComponent States\n.\n•\nSection 7.2 covers the core\nState Management\nrun-time responsibilities includ-\ning the start of\nApplications\n.\n•\nSection 7.3 describes what\nComponents\nand\nComponent States\nare and how\nthey are used.\n•\nSection 7.4 covers several topics related to\nAdaptive Diagnostics\nincluding\nshutdown prevention and executing of different reset types\n•\nSection 7.5 describes how\nUpdate and Config Management\ninteracts with\nState Management\n14 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P15_31",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 15,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n•\nSection 7.6 documents support provided by\nNetwork Management\nto de-\n/activate (partial) networks in dependency of\nFunction Group States\nand\nvice versa.\n•\nSection 7.7 describes how\nExecution Management\nis used to change\nFunc-\ntion Group State\nor\nMachine State\n.\n•\nSection 7.8 provides an introduction to how\nState Management\nwill work within\na virtualized environment.\n7.1 Technical Overview\nThis chapter presents a short summary of the relationship between\nState Manage-\nment\n, and all\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\nApplications which are mentioned in\nthe dependency section 5 of this document.\n7.1.1 Terms\nBefore discussing the concepts of\nOperational State\n,\nComponents\n, and\nCompo-\nnent States\nit is useful to present an overview of the terms so that the more detailed\ndiscussions have the required context.\nOperational State\n An internal state within\nState Management\nderived from mul-\ntiple events in the system. The\nOperational State\nmay be used to determine\nother states in the\nState Management\ne.g.\nComponent States\nand\nFunc-\ntion Group States\nComponent\n A\nProcess\nis comprised of one or more\nComponents\n.\nComponents\nare SW-entities that provide a particular function or group of related functions.\nComponent State\n\nComponent State\nis the internal state of\nComponents\n. It is\nused to enable Applications to be controlled in a more fine-grained way without\nthe need of restarting\nApplications\nwith a different parameter set.\nCompo-\nnent States\nare derived from\nOperational State\nor other project specific\nrequirements by\nState Managements\ninternal logic. At least ON and OFF state\nshall be supported.\nON\n full functionality provided.\nOFF\n no external functionality provided, all persisted data stored, ready to be\nterminated.\n15 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P16_32",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 16,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n7.2 State Management Responsibilities\nState Management\nis the functional cluster which is responsible for determining\nthe current\nOperational State\n, and for initiating\nFunction Group\nand\nMachine\nState\ntransitions by requesting them from\nExecution Management\n.\nState Management\ngrants full control over the set of\nApplications\nto be executed\nand ensures that\nProcesses\nare only executed (and hence resources allocated) when\nactually needed.\nState Management\nis the central point where any operation event is received that\nmight have an influence to the\nOperational State\n. The\nState Management\nis\nresponsible to evaluate these events and decide based on\n•\nEvent type (defined in project specific implementation based on project specific\nrequirements).\n•\nEvent priority (defined in project specific implementation based on project specific\nrequirements).\n•\nApplication identifier (Application identifier is not supported in this release. It is\nunder discussion with FT-SEC if such an identifier could be provided by\nIden-\ntity and Access Management\n).\nIf an\nOperational State\nchange is triggered\nExecution Management\nmay be\nrequested to set\nFunction Groups\nor\nMachine State\ninto new\nStates\n.\nThe state change request for\nFunction Groups\ncan be issued by several AUTOSAR\nApplications, e.g.:\n•\nPlatform Health Management\nto trigger error recovery, e.g. to activate fall-\nback Functionality\n•\nAdaptive Diagnostics\n, to switch the system into diagnostic states\n•\nUpdate and Config Management\nto switch the system into states where\nsoftware or configuration can be updated\n•\nNetwork Management\nto coordinate required functionality and network state\n•\nauthorized applications, e.g. a vehicle state manager which might be located in a\ndifferent machine or on a different ECU\nAUTOSAR Applications\nmay provide their own property or event via an ara com\ninterface, where the\nState Management\nis subscribing to, to trigger\nState Man-\nagement\ninternal events. Since\nState Management\nfunctionality is critical, access\nfrom other\nAUTOSAR Applications\nmust be secured, e.g. by\nIdentity and Ac-\ncess Management\n.\n•\nState Management\nmay be monitored and supervised by\nPlatform Health\nManagement\n.\n16 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P17_33",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 17,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n•\nState Management\nprovides interfaces to request information about current\nstates\nState Management\nis responsible for handling the following states:\n•\nMachine State see 7.2.1\n•\nFunction Group State see 7.2.2\n7.2.1 Machine State\nA\nMachine State\nis a specific type of\nFunction Group State\n(see 7.2.2).\nMa-\nchine States\nand all other\nFunction Group States\nare determined and re-\nquested by the\nState Management\nfunctional cluster, see 7.2.3. The set of active\nStates is significantly influenced by vehicle-wide events and modes which are evalu-\nated into\nState Managements\ninternal\nOperational States\n.\nThe\nFunction Group States\n, including the\nMachine State\n, define the current\nset of running\nProcesses\n. Each\nApplication\ncan declare in its\nExecution Man-\nifests\nin which\nFunction Group States\nits\nProcesses\nhave to be running.\nThe start-up sequence from initial state\nStartup\nto the point where\nState Manage-\nment\n,\nSM\n, requests the initial running machine state\nDriving\nis illustrated in Figure 7.1\nas an example\nDriving State\nis no mandatory\nState\n."

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\nAn arbitrary state change sequence to machine state\nStateXYZ\nis illustrated in Fig-\nure 7.2. Here, on receipt of the state change request,\nExecution Management\nter-\nminates running\nProcesses\nand then starts\nProcesses\nactive in the new state before\nconfirming the state change to\nState Management\n."

      "source_page": 18,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.2: State Change Sequence  Transition to machine state\nStateXYZ\n7.2.1.1 Startup\nExecution Management\nwill be controlled by\nState Management\nand therefore\nit should not execute any\nFunction Group State\nchanges on its own. This cre-\nates some expectations towards system configuration. The shall be done in this way\nthat\nState Management\nwill run in every\nMachine State\n(this includes\nStartup\n,\nShutdown\nand\nRestart\n). Above expectation is needed in order to ensure that there\nis always a software entity that can introduce changes in the current state of the\nMa-\nchine\n. If (for example) system integrator doesn't configure\nState Management\nto\nbe started in\nStartup Machine State\n, then\nMachine\nwill never be able transit to\nany other state and will be stuck forever in it. This also applies to any other\nMachine\nState\nstate that doesn't have\nState Management\nconfigured.\n18 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"

      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P19_36",

      "source_page": 19,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n7.2.1.2 Shutdown\nAs mentioned in 7.2.1.1 AUTOSAR assumes that\nState Management\nwill be config-\nured to run in\nShutdown\n. State transition is not a trivial system change and it can fail\nfor a number of reasons. When ever this happens you may want\nState Management\nto be still alive, so you can report an error and wait for further instructions. Please\nnote that very purpose of this state is to shutdown\nMachine\n(this includes\nState\nManagement\n) in a clean manner. Unfortunately this means that at some point\nState\nManagement\nwill no longer be available and it will not be able to report errors anymore.\nThose errors will be handled in a implementation specific way.\n7.2.1.3 Restart\nAs mentioned in 7.2.1.1 AUTOSAR assumes that\nState Management\nwill be config-\nured to run in\nRestart\n. The reasons for doing so are the same as for 7.2.1.2.\n7.2.2 Function Group State\nIf more than one group of functionally coherent\nApplications\nis installed on the\nsame machine, the\nMachine State\nmechanism is not flexible enough to control these\nfunctional clusters individually, in particular if they have to be started and terminated\nwith interleaving lifecycles. Many different\nMachine States\nwould be required in this\ncase to cover all possible combinations of active functional clusters.\nTo support this use case, additional\nFunction Groups\nand\nFunction Group\nStates\ncan be configured. Other use cases where starting and terminating individual\ngroups of\nProcesses\nmight be necessary including diagnostice and error recovery.\nIn general,\nMachine States\nare used to control machine lifecycle (startup/shut-\ndown/restart) and\nProcesses\nof platform level\nApplications\nwhile other\nFunction\nGroup States\nindividually control\nProcesses\nwhich belong to groups of functionally\ncoherent user level\nApplications\n.\n[SWS_SM_0001] Available Function Group (states)\n⌈\nState Management\nshall\nobtain available\nFunction Groups\nand their potential states from the\nMa-\nchine Manifest\nto set-up the\nFunction Group\nspecific state management.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00001)\nProcesses\nreference in their\nExecution Manifest\nthe states in which they want\nto be executed. A state can be any\nFunction Group State\n, including a\nMachine\nState\n. For details see [7], especially \"Mode-dependent Startup Configuration\" chapter\nand \"Function Groups\" chapter.\nThe arbitrary state change sequence as shown in Figure 7.2 applies to state changes of\nany\nFunction Group\n- just replace\n\"MachineState\"\nby the name of the\nFunction\nGroup\n. On receipt of the state change request,\nExecution Management\nterminates\n19 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\nnot longer needed\nProcesses\nand then starts\nProcesses\nactive in the new\nFunc-\ntion Group State\nbefore confirming the state change to\nState Management\n.\n[SWS_SM_0002] Function Group State Change Request\n⌈\nState Management\nshall implement functionality to enable\nAdaptive Applications\nand\nAdaptive\nPlatform Applications\nto change the\nFunction Group State\nof\nFunction\nGroups\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00001)\nIt might be that\nState Management\ndeclines or delays the request to change a\nFunction Group\ns state, based on\nState Management\ninternal\nOperational\nState\nor another\nAdaptive Application\nor\nAdaptive Platform Applica-\ntion\nwith higher priority that has the ownership of a\nFunction Group\n. As per cur-\nrent specification several\nAdaptive Applications\nor\nAdaptive Platform Ap-\nplications\nuse the service interface of\nState Management\ne.g.\nUpdate and\nConfig Management\nand a superior Function Group Manager. To ensure that the\ndecision to set\nFunction Groups\ninto a dedicated\nFunction Group State\nof a\nmore important application is not undermined by a less important application, the\napplication with a higher priority (project specific) get the ownership of the requested\nFunction Groups\nas long as it does not release the request.\n[SWS_SM_0003] Function Group State Retrieval\n⌈\nState Management\nshall im-\nplement functionality to enable\nAdaptive Applications\nand\nAdaptive Plat-\nform Applications\nto retrieve the\nFunction Group State\nof\nFunction\nGroups\nand\nState\nof\nMachine State\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00001)\n[SWS_SM_0004] Function Group State Change Request Result\n⌈\nState Man-\nagement\nshall return an appropriate result to the\nAdaptive Applications\nand\nAdaptive Platform Applications\nwhich has requested a\nFunction Group\nState\nchange.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00001)\nThe system might contain calibration data for variant handling. This might include that\nsome of the\nFunction Groups\nconfigured in the\nMachine Manifest\nare not in-\ntended to be executed on this system. therefore\nState Management\nhas to evaluate\ncalibration data to gather information about\nFunction Groups\nnot configured for the\nsystem variant\n[SWS_SM_0005] Function Group Calibration Support\n⌈\nState Management\nshall\nreceive information about deactivated\nFunction Groups\nfrom calibration data.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00300)\nThe storage and reception of calibration data is implementation specific.\n[SWS_SM_0006] Function Group Calibration Support\n⌈\nState Management\nshall\ndecline the request of\nAdaptive Applications\nand\nAdaptive Platform Ap-\nplications\nto change the\nFunction Group State\nof a\nFunction Group\nwhich\nis not configured to run in this variant.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00300)\n20 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"

      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P21_38",
      "source_element": null,

      "source_page": 21,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n7.2.3 State Management Architecture\nState Management\nis the functional cluster which is responsible for determining the\ncurrent set of active\nFunction Group States\n, including the\nMachine State\n, and\nfor initiating State transitions by requesting them from\nExecution Management\n.\nEx-\necution Management\nperforms the State transitions and controls the actual set of\nrunning\nProcesses\n, depending on the current States.\nState Management\nis the central point where new\nFunction Group States\ncan\nbe requested and where the requests are arbitrated, including coordination of contra-\ndicting requests from different sources. Additional data and events might need to be\nconsidered for arbitration.\nState Management\nfunctionality is highly project specific, and AUTOSAR decided\nagainst specifying functionality like the Classic Platforms BswM for the Adaptive Plat-\nform. It is planned to only specify set of basic service interfaces, and to encapsu-\nlate the actual arbitration logic into project specific code (e.g. a library), which can\nbe plugged into the\nState Management\nframework and has standardized interfaces\nbetween framework and arbitration logic, so the code can be reused on different plat-\nforms.\nThe arbitration logic code might be individually developed or (partly) generated, based\non standardized configuration parameters.\nAn overview of the interaction of\nState Management\n,\nExecution Management\nand\nApplications\nis shown in Figure 7.3.\n21 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P22_39",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 22,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P22_40",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 22,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.3: State Management Architecture\n7.3 State Management and Components\nPlease note that the term 'Component' is not yet finally decided and therefore subject\nof change!\nA single process is comprised of one or multiple\nComponents\n. A component is e.g.\na thread. To fulfill the needs of a resource optimized system it is necessary to control\nProcesss\nand therefore their\nComponents\nin a more fine-grained way than it is possi-\nble by\nExecution Management\n. When the internal behavior of a\nProcess\nshould be\nchanged by\nExecution Management\nit is needed to unload\nProcess\nfrom memory\n(including high latency due to persisting) and reload the\nExecutable\nfrom filesys-\ntem to memory. This behavior is resource consuming with respect to (flash-)memory\nbandwidth, CPU load and execution time.\nSo therefore\nComponents\nand their corresponding states are introduced. The\nCom-\nponent States\nare derived by\nState Management\nfrom internal\nOperational\nStates\nand from project specific requirements.\n22 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"
    },

      "source_page": 23,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\nOne important use-case is the 'late-wakeup', where a new wakeup reason is found\nduring a running shutdown. With the current approach the shutdown can't be inter-\nrupted and all\nProcesss\nhave to be unloaded and newly loaded. With the\nCompo-\nnent States\nit is possible to switch all\nComponents\nto their 'OFF' state, where all\ne.g. persisting should be done (like when a\nProcess\ngets termination request from\nExecution Management\n), but they will stay in memory and can continue their work\nimmediately when they are set into\nComponent State\n'ON' again by\nState Man-\nagement\n.\n[SWS_SM_0010] Component (states)\n⌈\nState Management\nshall enable\nPro-\ncesses\nto change their internal behavior without the need of being reloaded.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00002)\n[SWS_SM_0011] Component (states) Handling\n⌈\nState Management\nshall cal-\nculate\nComponent States\nfrom current\nOperational State\nand other project\nspecific requirements and send the state to the registered\nComponents\n.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00002)\nTo enable\nComponents\nto receive\nComponent States\nthey have to register at\nState Manager\nvia its API interface (see section 8.2 API function definition). When\nComponents\nare not longer interested in receiving\nComponent States\nthey have to\nun-register form\nState Manager\n, thus these\nComponents\nare removed from\nState\nManager\ns internal list. Registration is done by calling the consturctor of Component-\nClient, un-registration is done by calling its destructor.\n[SWS_SM_0012] Component (states) Registration\n⌈\nState Management\nshall\nprovide means to\nComponents\nto register / un-register for receiving\nComponent\nStates\n.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00002)\nComponents\nare allowed to temporary delay the next provided\nComponent State\nwhen it sees a reason to do so (e.g. an OFF state might be delayed due to an ongoing\nphone call). therefore each\nComponent\nhas to confirm that it has received the request\nto enter a new\nComponent State\n. This confirmation shall contain the current state\n(either the requested one or the previous one) of the\nComponent\nand a result. For\ndetails see section 8.2.1.5. When the transition to the requested state is delayed\nState\nManagement\nretries to request the\nComponent State\nafter a configured timeout has\nexceeded. This retry shall be done a configured number of times. Timeout values and\nretry counts shall be retrieved from\nExecution Manifest\n[SWS_SM_0013] Component (states) Configuration\n⌈\nState Management\nshall\nretrieve configuration parameters for\nComponents\nfrom\nExecution Manifest\n.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00002)\n[SWS_SM_0014] Component (states) Enforcement\n⌈\nState Management\nshall\nforce to enter a\nComponent State\nwhen the configured retry count and timeout val-\nues are exceeded.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00002)\n[SWS_SM_0015] Component (states) Transitions\n⌈\nComponents\nmust be able to\nperform a transition from any\nComponent State\ninto any\nComponent State\nthat\nthey have defined.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00002)\n23 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"

      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P24_42",
      "source_element": "SWS_SM_0100",

      "source_page": 24,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\nComponent States\nare used in conjunction with\nAdaptive Diagnostics\nto im-\nplement means to handle reset requests. For further details see section 7.4.\n7.4 Interaction with Adaptive Diagnostics\nAdaptive Diagnostics\nis responsible for diagnosing and configuring and reset-\nting\nFunction Groups\n. During any diagnostic is executed it is necessary to prevent\nsystem from shutting down.\n[SWS_SM_0100] Prevent Shutdown due to Diagnostic Session\n⌈\nState Manage-\nment\nshall not shutdown the system during an active diagnostic session. Therefore\nState Management\nhas to register to\nAdaptive Diagnostics\nto receive informa-\ntion about active diagnostic session\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00100)\nFrom\nAdaptive Diagnostics\npoint of view several different reset types have to be\ncarried out to fulfill functionality of\nAdaptive Diagnostics\n. Because the interpreta-\ntion of the reset types (defined in ISO 14229-1)\n•\nhardReset\n•\nkeyOffOnReset\n•\nsoftReset\nis done differently by each OEM, parts of the reset functionality have to be delegated\nby\nState Management\nto\nAdaptive Applications\nand\nAdaptive Platform\nApplications\n.\nHere the\nComponent States\ncomes into scope again: The reset types may be car-\nried out by application when the following reset types are 'translated' by\nState Man-\nagements\ninternal project specific logic to\nComponent States\n•\nhardReset\n•\nsoftReset\nThe functionality behind this states is highly\nAdaptive Application\nspecific. When\nan\nAdaptive Application\nsees no need to support such functionality this states\nmay be skipped immediately. A 'hardReset' could be interpreted e.g. that an\nAdap-\ntive Application\nhas to reset its related hardware(e.g. a tuner application may\nreset the tuner hardware by means of the tuner driver). A 'softReset' may be inter-\npreted e.g. that an\nAdaptive Application\nhas to load its default configuration.\nA 'keyOffOnReset' may be translated by\nState Managements\ninternal logic to stop\nand start the provided\nFunction Groups\n.\nPlease note that this behavior is currently under discussion and therefore subject of\nchange!\n[SWS_SM_0101] Diagnostic Reset\n⌈\nState Management\nshall implement means\nto receive reset requests for\nFunction Groups\nfrom\nAdaptive Diagnostics\n.\n24 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P25_43",
      "source_element": "SWS_SM_0102",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 25,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\nState Management\nshall carry out the project specific actions for the specific reset\ntype\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00100)\n[SWS_SM_0102] Component States for Reset\n⌈\nState Management\nshall provide\nfunctionality to enable\nComponents\nto implement means to execute specific reset\ntypes by using\nComponent States\n.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00100, RS_SM_00002)\nThe\nFunction Group Machine State\nhas to be handled in a different way when\nexecuting reset requests from\nAdaptive Diagnostics\n: A 'hardReset' could be in-\nterpreted e.g. that an\nAdaptive Application\nhas to be launched (by requesting\ne.g.\nFunction Group\n'reset' from\nExecution Management\n) which carries out the\nOS or hardware specific reset. A 'softReset' could be interpreted by shutting down\nall\nFunction Groups\nand requesting a\nMachine State\n'restart' from\nExecution\nManagement\n.\nBut this functionality is project-specific, too. So therefore the correct mapping has to\nbe done by the OEM code, too.\nState Management\nis the central point in the system, where a reset for the\nMachine\ncould be requested. So\nState Management\nhas to keep track of reset causes and\nhas to reset the persistent reset cause when it is newly spawned.\n[SWS_SM_0103] Diagnostic Reset Last Cause\n⌈\nState Management\nshall provide\nfunctionality to persist reset type before\nMachine\nreset is carried.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00100,\nRS_SM_00101)\n[SWS_SM_0104] Diagnostic Reset Last Cause Retrieval\n⌈\nState Management\nshall read out the last persisted reset cause when\nState Management\nis spawned.\nThis reset cause has to be provided via its service interface\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00100,\nRS_SM_00101)\n[SWS_SM_0105] Diagnostic Reset Last Cause Reset\n⌈\nState Management\nshall\nreset the last persisted reset cause immediately after\nState Management\nhas read\nout the current value.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00100, RS_SM_00101)\n7.5 Interaction with Update and Config Management\nUpdate and Config Management\nis responsible for updating\nFunction\nGroups\n,\nManifests\n(execution or machine manifest) or the whole\nAUTOSAR\nAdaptive Platform\n. During any update is executed it is necessary to prevent\nsystem from shutting down.\n[SWS_SM_0200] Prevent Shutdown due to Update Session\n⌈\nState Manage-\nment\nshall not shutdown the system during an update session is active. therefore\nState Management\nhas to register to\nUpdate and Config Management\nto re-\nceive information about active update session\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00100)\nTo enable\nUpdate and Config Management\nto fulfill its functionality an update and\na verify state should be available in the\nManifests\nfor each\nFunction Group\nand\n25 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"

      "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P26_44",
      "source_element": "SWS_SM_0201",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\nfor\nMachine State\n.\nUpdate and Config Management\nhas to request the corre-\nsponding\nFunction Group State\nfrom\nState Management\n.\n[SWS_SM_0201] Reset Execution\n⌈\nState Management\nshall implement means\nto issue a\nMachine\nreset when\nMachine State\nchanges from\nFunction Group\nState\n'update' to 'verify'.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00100)\nIn case of an update of an\nAdaptive Applications\nwhich does not imply an ECU/-\nmachine reset (i.e. soft reset),\nExecution Management\nneeds to be triggered to\nreparse the\nManifests\n(execution or machine manifest) of this\nAdaptive Appli-\ncation\nprior to restarting it (in order to start it with the right (i.e updated) configuration).\nOtherwise\nExecution Management\nwould only reparse the processed\nManifests\nduring the next ECU/machine reset (which is too late). For that purpose, an additional\ninterface is needed between\nUpdate and Config Management\n,\nState Manage-\nment\nand\nExecution Management\n.\n7.6 Interaction with Network Management\nTo be portable between different ECUs the\nAdaptive Applications\nshould not\nhave the need to know which networks are needed to fulfill its functionality, because on\ndifferent ECUs the networks could be configured differently. To control the availability of\nnetworks for several\nAdaptive Applications State Management\ninteracts with\nNetwork Management\nvia a service interface. For details see section 9.3.3.\nNetwork Management\nprovides multiple instances of NetworkHandles, where each\nrepresents a set of (partial) networks.\nThe NetworkHandles are defined in the\nMachine Manifest\nand are there assigned\nto a\nFunction Group State\n.\n[SWS_SM_0300] NetworkHandle Configuration\n⌈\nState Management\nshall re-\nceive information about NetworkHandles and their associated\nFunction Group\nStates\nfrom\nMachine Manifest\n.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00400)\nWhenever (partial) networks are activated or deactivated from outside request and this\nset of (partial) networks is represented by a NetworkHandle in\nMachine Manifest\nNetwork Management\nwill change the value of the corresponding NetworkHandle.\nState Management\nis notified about the change, because it has registered to all\navailabe NetworkHandle fields. When\nState Management\nrecognizes a change in\na fields value it sets the corresponding\nFunction Group\nin the\nFunction Group\nState\nwhere the NetworkHandle is configured for in the\nMachine Manifest\n.\n[SWS_SM_0301] NetworkHandle Registration\n⌈\nState Management\nshall register\nfor all NetworkHandles provided by\nNetwork Managements\nwhich are available from\nMachine Manifest\n.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00400)\n[SWS_SM_0302] NetworkHandle to FunctionGroupState\n⌈\nState Management\nshall set\nFunction Groups\nto the corresponding\nFunction Group State\nwhich\n26 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\nis configured in the\nMachine Manifest\nfor the NetworkHandle when it recognizes a\nchange in NetworkHandle value.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00400)\nVice versa\nState Managements\nshall change the value of the NetworkHandle when\na\nFunction Group\nhas to change its\nFunction Group State\nand an associa-\ntion between this\nFunction Group State\nand the Network handle is available in\nMachine Manifest\n.\nNetwork Management\nwill recognize this change and will\nchange the state of the (partial) networks accordingly to the NetworkHandle.\n[SWS_SM_0303] FunctionGroupState to NetworkHandle\n⌈\nState Management\nshall change the value of NetworkHandle when\nFunction Groups\nchanges its\nFunction Group State\nand a NetworkHandle is associated to this\nFunction\nGroup State\nin the\nMachine Manifest\n.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00400)\nIt might be needed that a\nFunction Group\nstays longer in its\nFunction Group\nState\nwhen the causing (partial) network set has been switched off or a (partial) net-\nwork is longer available than the causing\nFunction Group\nhas been switched to\nFunction Group State\n'Off'. This is called 'afterrun'. The corresponding timeout-\nvalue has to be configured in\nMachine Manifest\n[SWS_SM_0304] Network Afterrun\n⌈\nState Management\nshall support means to\nsupport 'afterrun' to switch off related\nFunction Groups\nor (partial) networks. The\ntimeout value for this 'afterrun' has to be read from e.g.\nMachine Manifest\n.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00400)\n7.7 Interaction with Execution Management\nExecution Management\nis used to execute the the\nFunction Group State\nchanges. The decision to change the\nState\nof\nMachine State\nor the\nFunction\nGroup State\nof\nFunction Groups\nmight come from inside of\nState Manage-\nment\nbased on\nOperational State\n(or other project specific requirements) or might\nbe requested at\nState Management\nfrom an external\nAdaptive Application\n.\n[SWS_SM_0400] Execution Management\n⌈\nState Management\nshall use API of\nExecution Management\nto change the\nState\nof\nMachine State\nor\nFunction\nGroup State\nof\nFunction Groups\n.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00001)\nExecution Management\nmight not be able to carry out the requested\nFunction\nGroup State\nchange due to several reasons (e.g. corrupted binary).\nExecution\nManagement\nreturns the result of the request.\n[SWS_SM_0401] Execution Management Results\n⌈\nState Management\nshall\nevaluate the results of request to\nExecution Management\n. Based on this results\nState Management\nmight decide to do further actions\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00001)\n[SWS_SM_0402] Function Group State CHange Results\n⌈\nState Management\nshall provide\nFunction Group States\nbased on the results of\nFunction Group\n27 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\nState\nchange requests to\nExecution Management\nvia its service interface\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00001)\n7.8 State Management in a virtualized environment\nOn an ECU several machines might run in a virtualized environment. Each of the\nvirtual machines might contain an AUTOSAR Adaptive platform. So therefore each\nof the virtual machines contain\nState Management\n. To have coordinated control\nover the several virtual machines there has to be virtual machine which supervises the\nwhole ECU state.\n[SWS_SM_0500] Virtualized State Management\n⌈\nState Management\nshall be\nable to register to a supervising\nState Management\ninstance to receive information\nabout the whole ECU state.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00200, RS_SM_00201)\n[SWS_SM_0501] Virtualized State Management Operational State\n⌈\nState Man-\nagement\nshall implement means to calculate its\nOperational State\nbased on\ninformation from a supervising\nState Management\ninstance.\n⌋\n(RS_SM_00200,\nRS_SM_00201)\n28 of 40\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 908: AUTOSAR_SWS_StateManagement"

Für Suspend-to-RAM koordiniert <code>S2RHub</code> registrierte <code>S2RSatellite</code>-Instanzen; die Plattform-Erweiterung koppelt OS-Power-State und Wake-up-Handler. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.5\">SWS StateManagement §7.5 „Suspend-to-RAM“</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00710\">[SWS_SM_00710]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00711\">[SWS_SM_00711]</a></p>\n<h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall</h4>\n<p>Der Fehlerbereich <code>SmErrorDomain</code> definiert <code>SmErrc::kRejected</code> für Probleme eines S2R-Satelliten beim Betreten oder Verlassen des Suspend-Modus. Davon getrennt beschreibt der Typ <code>UpdateStatusType</code> die Fortschrittswerte des Update-Dienstes: <code>kRejected</code> für eine Anforderung außerhalb einer Update-Session und <code>kFailed</code> für eine fehlgeschlagene Verarbeitung. <code>ResetMachineNotifier</code> ist dafür ein Feld mit Getter und Notifier; State Management setzt es, um UCM während und nach <code>ResetMachine()</code> zu informieren. <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_81240\">[SWS_SM_81240]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_91027\">[SWS_SM_91027]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_91106\">[SWS_SM_91106]</a></p>\n<p>Für den StateMachine-Pfad wird ein <code>ExecutionError</code> von Execution Management (über <code>GetExecutionError()</code> oder <code>undefinedStateCallback</code>) oder von Platform Health Management (über den RecoveryHandler) als ErrorCode der StateMachine verwendet, die die betroffene Function Group verwaltet. Bei einer nicht als <code>ImpactedByUpdate</code> markierten StateMachine setzt State Management die laufende Fehlerbehandlung, wertet die <code>ErrorRecoveryTable</code> aus, beendet die bisherige ActionList-Verarbeitung und wechselt unmittelbar in den konfigurierten Folgezustand. Für nicht explizit gemappte Fehler ist ein <code>ANY</code>-Eintrag verpflichtend. <a class=\"swsref\" <p><code>ara::sm</code> bestimmt Machine- und Function-Group-Zustände; die konkrete Prozessführung erfolgt über Execution Management. Damit trennt das Konzept die fachliche Entscheidung über einen Zielzustand von Start, Stopp und Reihenfolge der Prozesse. <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00400">[SWS_SM_00400]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.1">SWS StateManagement §7.1 „Responsibilities“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.6">SWS StateManagement §7.6 „Interaction with Execution Management“</a></p>
<h4>Konfigurierbare Zustandsmaschinen</h4>
<p>Eine StateMachine bündelt Zustände, Transitionen und ActionLists. Eine steuernde Anwendung fordert einen Übergang an; Zustandsbenachrichtigungen erlauben anderen Anwendungen, den aktuellen Zustand zu beobachten. Der Controller ist pro StateMachine-Konfiguration eindeutig. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.7">SWS StateManagement §7.7 „StateMachine“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00619">[SWS_SM_00619]</a></p>

<h4>Update-Sitzung als Zustandskoordination</h4>
<p>UCM beginnt die Zusammenarbeit über <code>RequestUpdateSession()</code>. Danach führen <code>PrepareUpdate</code>, <code>VerifyUpdate</code> und bei Bedarf <code>PrepareRollback</code> betroffene StateMachines in die dafür konfigurierten Zustände. Die Entscheidung, ob ein Update zulässig ist, ist projektspezifisch und hängt vom Maschinen- oder Fahrzeugzustand ab. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.3">SWS StateManagement §7.3 „Interaction with UCM“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.7.14">SWS StateManagement §7.7.14 „StateMachine support for UCM“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00206">[SWS_SM_00206]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00207">[SWS_SM_00207]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00208">[SWS_SM_00208]</a></p>

<h4>Integrationsgrenzen und Zusatzpfade</h4>
<p>Der Zugriff auf <code>UpdateRequest</code> ist durch Identity and Access Management auf UCM zu begrenzen. Für Suspend-to-RAM koordiniert <code>S2RHub</code> registrierte <code>S2RSatellite</code>-Instanzen; die Plattform-Erweiterung koppelt OS-Power-State und Wake-up-Handler. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.5">SWS StateManagement §7.5 „Suspend-to-RAM“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00710">[SWS_SM_00710]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00711">[SWS_SM_00711]</a></p>
<h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall</h4>
<p>Der Fehlerbereich <code>SmErrorDomain</code> definiert <code>SmErrc::kRejected</code> für Probleme eines S2R-Satelliten beim Betreten oder Verlassen des Suspend-Modus. Davon getrennt beschreibt der Typ <code>UpdateStatusType</code> die Fortschrittswerte des Update-Dienstes: <code>kRejected</code> für eine Anforderung außerhalb einer Update-Session und <code>kFailed</code> für eine fehlgeschlagene Verarbeitung. <code>ResetMachineNotifier</code> ist dafür ein Feld mit Getter und Notifier; State Management setzt es, um UCM während und nach <code>ResetMachine()</code> zu informieren. <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_81240">[SWS_SM_81240]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_91027">[SWS_SM_91027]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_91106">[SWS_SM_91106]</a></p>
<p>Für den StateMachine-Pfad wird ein <code>ExecutionError</code> von Execution Management (über <code>GetExecutionError()</code> oder <code>undefinedStateCallback</code>) oder von Platform Health Management (über den RecoveryHandler) als ErrorCode der StateMachine verwendet, die die betroffene Function Group verwaltet. Bei einer nicht als <code>ImpactedByUpdate</code> markierten StateMachine setzt State Management die laufende Fehlerbehandlung, wertet die <code>ErrorRecoveryTable</code> aus, beendet die bisherige ActionList-Verarbeitung und wechselt unmittelbar in den konfigurierten Folgezustand. Für nicht explizit gemappte Fehler ist ein <code>ANY</code>-Eintrag verpflichtend. <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00670">[SWS_SM_00670]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00601">[SWS_SM_00601]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014">[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014]</a></p>

<p>Fehler eines <code>StateClient::SetState()</code>-Aufrufs mit <code>ExecErrc::kNoCommunication</code>, <code>kInvalidTransition</code> oder <code>kInvalidMetaModelIdentifier</code> werden auf den konfigurierten <code>functionGroupTransitionRequestFailedError</code> abgebildet; ohne Konfiguration ist der Fehlerwert <code>1</code> zu verwenden. Beim Update kann <code>RequestUpdateSession()</code> wegen des Maschinenzustands mit <code>kOperationRejected</code> abgelehnt werden; während bereits eine Session aktiv ist, ist <code>kNotAllowedMultipleUpdateSessions</code> vorgeschrieben. <code>ResetMachine()</code> wird ohne zuvor erfolgreich angeforderte Update-Session abgewiesen und setzt außerhalb einer Update-Session den <code>ResetMachineNotifier</code> auf <code>kRejected</code>. Misslingt nach einem Reset der Übergang nach <code>ContinueUpdate</code>, ist <code>kFailed</code> zu setzen. <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00671">[SWS_SM_00671]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00672">[SWS_SM_00672]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_91102">[SWS_SM_91102]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_91100">[SWS_SM_91100]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00661">[SWS_SM_00661]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00663">[SWS_SM_00663]</a></p>

Für Suspend-to-RAM koordiniert <code>S2RHub</code> registrierte <code>S2RSatellite</code>-Instanzen; die Plattform-Erweiterung koppelt OS-Power-State und Wake-up-Handler. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.5">SWS StateManagement §7.5 „Suspend-to-RAM“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00710">[SWS_SM_00710]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_00711">[SWS_SM_00711]</a></p> <h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall</h4> <p>Der Fehlerbereich <code>SmErrorDomain</code> definiert <code>SmErrc::kRejected</code> für Probleme eines S2R-Satelliten beim Betreten oder Verlassen des Suspend-Modus. Davon getrennt beschreibt der Typ <code>UpdateStatusType</code> die Fortschrittswerte des Update-Dienstes: <code>kRejected</code> für eine Anforderung außerhalb einer Update-Session und <code>kFailed</code> für eine fehlgeschlagene Verarbeitung. <code>ResetMachineNotifier</code> ist dafür ein Feld mit Getter und Notifier; State Management setzt es, um UCM während und nach <code>ResetMachine()</code> zu informieren. <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_81240">[SWS_SM_81240]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_91027">[SWS_SM_91027]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_SM_91106">[SWS_SM_91106]</a></p> <p>Für den StateMachine-Pfad wird ein <code>ExecutionError</code> von Execution Management (über <code>GetExecutionError()</code> oder <code>undefinedStateCallback</code>) oder von Platform Health Management (über den RecoveryHandler) als ErrorCode der StateMachine verwendet, die die betroffene Function Group verwaltet. Bei einer nicht als <code>ImpactedByUpdate</code> markierten StateMachine setzt State Management die laufende Fehlerbehandlung, wertet die <code>ErrorRecoveryTable</code> aus, beendet die bisherige ActionList-Verarbeitung und wechselt unmittelbar in den konfigurierten Folgezustand. Für nicht explizit gemappte Fehler ist ein <code>ANY</code>-Eintrag verpflichtend. <a class="swsref" 1 Introduction and functional overview
This document is the software specification of the
State Management
functional
cluster within the
Adaptive Platform Services
.
State Management
is responsible for determination of the overall operation state of
the Adaptive AUTOSAR Platform. Additionally
State Management
takes care to set
Components
into an internal
Component State
which depends on the determined
Operational State
and on other project specific requirements. The idea behind
Component States
is to control
Processs
in a more fine-grained way without the
need of restarting them with a different set of command-line parameters.
State Management
interacts with the
Execution Management
to request
Func-
tion Groups
and the
Machine State
to enter specific states that are determined
to project requirements.
Chapter 7 describes how
State Management
concepts are realized within the
Adap-
tive Platform
.
Chapter 8 documents the State Management Application Programming Interface (API).
1.1 What is State Management?
State Management
is the functional cluster within the
Adaptive Platform Ser-
vices
that is responsible to determine the operation state, based on information re-
ceived or gathered from other
Adaptive Platform
Applications or Adaptive Appli-
cations.
1.2 Interaction with AUTOSAR Runtime for Adaptive
The set of programming interfaces to the Adaptive Applications is called AUTOSAR
Runtime for Adaptive (ARA). The interfaces that constitute ARA include those of
State
Management
specified in Chapter 8 . Note that APIs accessed by
State Manage-
ment
using the inter-functional cluster API that is described in Appendix A which is
not part of ARA.
The Adaptive AUTOSAR Services are provided via mechanisms provided by the
Com-
munication Management
functional cluster [1] of the Adaptive Platform Foundation

provides information about an ongoing diagnostics

to prevent shutdown
of the system when a diagnostics session is ongoing.

provides information about
an ongoing update session. This information is evaluated by

to
prevent shutdown of the system when an update session is ongoing.

Specification of State Management
AUTOSAR AP Release 18-10
7 Functional specification
State Management
is a functional cluster contained in the
Adaptive Platform
Services
.
State Management
is responsible for all aspects of Operation
State
Management
including handling of incoming events or requests, prioritization of these
events/requests and setting the
Operational State
. The
State Management
can also register to properties of other Adaptive Platform or
Adaptive Applica-
tions
to be informed about changes. These changes can also trigger a transition in
the
Operational State
machine.
Additionally the
State Management
takes care of not shutting down the system as
long as any diagnostic or update session is active as part of its internal
Operational
